_comment: §6.N bluff-hunt CYCLE 2 — lava-api-go (Go) ONLY. 5 PRE-EXISTING *_test.go files across 5 distinct packages/layers, NONE authored this session (explicitly excluded: search_telemetry_test.go, capability_honesty_test.go, catalogue_parity_test.go, search_chaos_deadline_test.go, the search/multisearch deadline tests, and cycle-1's internal/auth/backoff_test.go). For each target: the EXACT production function the test claims to cover was deliberately MUTATED, ONLY the scoped single test(s) were run via `go test -run`, the verbatim FAIL captured, then the mutation reverted via `git checkout --` and the scoped test re-run to confirm GREEN. All mutations reverted; git status clean of production-file mutations at end. No bluffs found. NO adb/emulator/device/gradle used; no git add/commit/push.
cycle: cycle-2 (lava-api-go Go-only), parallel to the main Android stream's §6.AK device-gate work
toolchain: go test (separate toolchain from the in-use Android Gradle)
constraints: scoped single-package single-test Go unit tests only (`go test ./<pkg>/ -run '<TestName>'`); NO adb/emulator/device, NO :app gradle, NO full-project build, NO git add/commit/push. Reverts polled the concurrent main stream's .git/index.lock (NEVER removed it) and retried git checkout once the lock cleared.

targets.claims_to_cover: the valid-value branch: when LAVA_API_* env var parses to a valid time.Duration, the PARSED value (not the default) is the value the server runs with; covers timeouts/retentions like LAVA_API_SEARCH_TIMEOUT
targets.mutation: in envDuration, the valid-parse branch `return d` -> `_ = d; return def` (silently drop the parsed value so the default always wins even when the operator set a valid value)
targets.observed_failure_verbatim:
--- FAIL: TestEnvDuration_ValidValueWins (0.00s)
    env_helpers_test.go:25: envDuration valid: got 5s, want 1.5s
FAIL  digital.vasic.lava.apigo/internal/config 0.412s  (the garbage-returns-default test stayed PASS — mutation localized to the valid-value path)

targets.claims_to_cover: the binary (1024) byte->human-string conversion shown in every Jackett-backed search/browse/topic result (e.g. 1 KB, 1.5 MB, 2 GB, 3 TB...); a wrong multiplier shows a user a wrong size
targets.observed_failure_verbatim: --- FAIL: TestHumanSize/exactly_one_KB: humansize_test.go:51: humanSize(1024) = "1.02 KB", want "1.00 KB"  (plus just_under_a_KB "1.02 KB" want "1023 B", one_and_a_half_MB "1.57 MB" want "1.50 MB", two_GB "2.15 GB" want "2.00 GB", three_TB "3.30 TB" want "3.00 TB", five_PB + two_EB likewise). FAIL digital.vasic.lava.apigo/internal/provider/jackettprovider

targets.production_function: parseHumanSize / sizeUnits (the IEC suffix->byte multiplier table)
targets.claims_to_cover: Nyaa human size string ('400 MiB') -> exact bytes, surfaced as the user-visible SearchItem.SizeBytes from the real RSS parse path
targets.mutation: sizeUnits MiB multiplier `{"MiB", 1 << 20}` -> `{"MiB", 1 << 10}` (MiB folded to KiB scale)
targets.observed_failure_verbatim:
--- FAIL: TestSearch_ParsesFixture (0.01s)
    nyaa_test.go:79: sizeBytes = 409600, want 419430400 (400 MiB)
FAIL  digital.vasic.lava.apigo/internal/provider/curated/nyaa

targets.layer: QA validator adapter (Go; HelixQA Detector+Validator+ticket Generator are real instances, CommandRunner mocked at the boundary below the SUT per §6.J clause 4)
targets.claims_to_cover: on a FAILED step with auto-emit wired, a real §6.O markdown ticket file is written to disk (asserted as a real .md file on disk containing the step name + test-case ID), not just a call count
targets.mutation: the auto-emit guard `if v.autoEmit && v.hxqaTkt != nil {` -> `if false && v.autoEmit && v.hxqaTkt != nil {` (never emit the ticket on a failed step)
targets.observed_failure_verbatim:
--- FAIL: TestValidateStep_FailedWithAutoEmit_WritesTicket (0.03s)
    validator_test.go:253: ticket dir has 0 entries; want 1
FAIL  digital.vasic.lava.apigo/internal/qa/validator  (the PassedWithAutoEmit_NoTicketEmitted test stayed PASS — mutation localized to the failure-emit path)

targets.layer: cache-key derivation (Go, pure logic; security-relevant — cross-tenant cache isolation)
targets.production_function: Key(method, routeTemplate, pathVars, query, authRealmHash) string
targets.claims_to_cover: the auth realm hash is part of the cache key so two distinct authenticated users (user-A vs user-B) get DISTINCT keys — prevents cross-user cache poisoning where one user is served another user's cached response
targets.mutation: in the raw sha256 input slice, the trailing `authRealmHash,` element -> `"",` (drop the realm from the key material so every realm collides)
targets.observed_failure_verbatim:
--- FAIL: TestKeyDistinguishesAuthRealm (0.00s)
    cache_test.go:33: Key collided across distinct auth realms
FAIL  digital.vasic.lava.apigo/internal/cache  (TestKeyAnonDefault — empty realm == 'anon' — stayed PASS; mutation localized to the realm-distinguishing path)
